problem: A metal plate occupies the region $D={(x,y):-1\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le {y}^{2}}.$ The charge density of the plate is given by $\rho (x,y)=x{y}^{2}.$ Find the total charge $Q$ of the plate.

activity_context.topic_title: Density, Mass, and Charge of Plane Laminas

feedback.problem: Find the total charge $Q$ of the lower half of the circular disk ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 9$ with charge density function $\rho $ given by $\rho (x,y)=y$
feedback.worked_solution:
The total charge $Q$ of  the lower half of the circular disk  $D={(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 9,\,y\le 0}$ with charge density $\rho (x,y)=y$ is given by

$$
Q={∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since $y\le 0,$ we obtain

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 9\,⟹\,y\ge -\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066271/assets/af77552bd144fb70dfe8787060c0136f54955d20cdd2543391bd040b01a460d2.png)

Notice that $D$ is a type I region.

- We already know the intersection of the circle with the line $y=0.$ So, the $x$-limits are $-3\le x\le 3.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066271/assets/32db7009737aa47c8b5a96da91d72b0db95530271f463a9f7d35f715793cbea8.png)

As a result, the integral is defined over the following type I region:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-3\le x\le 3,\,-\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}}\le y\le 0}
$$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
{∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A={\int }_{-3}^{3}{\int }_{-\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}}}^{0}y\,dy\,dx
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}[{\int }_{-\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}}}^{0}y\,dy]\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{-\sqrt{9-{x}^{2}}}^{0}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}(0-\frac{9-{x}^{2}}{2})\,dx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-3}^{3}({x}^{2}-9)\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-3}^{3}({x}^{2}-9)\,dx & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-9x]}_{-3}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[(9-27)-(-9+27)] \\  & =-18\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the total charge of the lower half of the circular disk is $Q=-18.$
